name: Add-on
blurb: a lean core price, with the real margin in the extras customers add on. Ryanair, Best Buy, American Airlines.

name: All-you-can-use / Flat-rate
blurb: one price for unlimited use; a bet that average consumption stays below the fee. Spotify, Netflix, Peloton, AT&T.

name: Freemium
blurb: give the basics away, charge for the powerful tier; convert enough free users and it compounds. Slack, Zoom, Spotify, Alphabet.

name: Pay-per-use
blurb: charge only for what's consumed, aligning cost to value. AWS, Twilio, utilities.

name: Outcome / Performance-based
blurb: sell the result, not the tool; get paid when the customer's goal lands. ad networks, modern AI agents.

name: Razor-and-blade
blurb: sell the platform cheap, profit on the consumables (or the reverse). printers/ink, razors, consoles/games.

name: Robin Hood
blurb: charge the high end more to subsidize serving the low end; widen the market without abandoning premium. tiered SaaS, some healthcare.

name: Ultra-luxury / Premium
blurb: turn scarcity and exclusivity into the model itself. Hermès, Ferrari, Patek Philippe.

name: Usage-based / AI-metered
blurb: meter units of AI work (token → action → conversation → resolution → outcome). foundation-model APIs, Intercom Fin, Agentforce, Sierra. → deep profile in `01-business-models-sample.md`.

name: Fractional ownership
blurb: share a high-value asset instead of buying it whole. NetJets, Marriott Vacations, Masterworks.

name: Asset sharing / Utilization
blurb: monetize idle capacity by renting it out. Airbnb, Turo, WeWork.

name: Rental / Product-as-service
blurb: rent repeatedly instead of selling once; recurring revenue from durable goods. Rent the Runway, tool rental.

name: Subscription / Access
blurb: trade ownership for ongoing access and predictable revenue. Adobe, Netflix, gyms.

name: Product-as-a-Service (circular)
blurb: customer pays for use/outcome; provider keeps ownership and handles the lifecycle. Signify (light-as-service), Michelin tires-as-service.

name: Affiliate / Referral
blurb: sell the ability to sell; partners earn a cut, you gain reach without a sales force. Booking.com, eBay, Mastercard.

name: Peer-to-peer
blurb: the trusted middleman connecting like individuals. eBay, LendingClub, Chess.com.

name: Two-sided platform / Marketplace
blurb: connect two groups that need each other and become the essential intermediary. Airbnb, Uber, Alibaba.

name: Orchestrator / Coordinator
blurb: conduct the value chain instead of owning it. Nike (outsourced production), Li & Fung.

name: Creator monetization
blurb: aggregate an audience; monetize creator content via ads, subs, tips, revenue share, and take a cut. YouTube, Substack, TikTok.

name: Digitization
blurb: take something physical and make it digital: faster, cheaper, infinitely scalable. Spotify, Adobe, NYT.

name: E-commerce
blurb: the store that never closes; sell online, shed retail overhead. Alibaba, Shopify, Wayfair.

name: Data monetization / Data-driven
blurb: turn the information you generate into a product. Google, Bloomberg, credit bureaus.

name: Data-as-a-Service / IoT data
blurb: sell the insight the sensors produce, not the hardware. John Deere precision-ag, Bloomberg Terminal.

name: Digitization of physical processes
blurb: replicate a physical workflow in software, removing physical constraints. DocuSign, telemedicine.

name: Point-of-use / Embedded purchase
blurb: move the buy decision to the moment of need. embedded finance, BNPL at checkout.

name: Blockchain-as-a-Service
blurb: offer blockchain infrastructure so others build without running it. cloud BaaS offerings.

name: Contrarian / Opposite positioning
blurb: do the diametric opposite of the industry norm and win the customers tired of it. Uber, Netflix, Airbnb.

name: Direct sales / Network sales
blurb: cut the middleman; own the customer relationship and the margin. Chanel, Ford, Tupperware.

name: Direct-to-Consumer (DTC)
blurb: brand sells straight to end customers online, owning relationship and margin. Warby Parker, Dollar Shave Club, Casper.

name: Shop-in-shop
blurb: place your store inside someone else's footprint and borrow their traffic. brand counters, Target/Ulta.

name: Ingredient branding
blurb: make your component so desirable that finished products advertise it. Intel Inside, Gore-Tex, Dolby.

name: Licensing / IP
blurb: create the intellectual property; let others manufacture. ARM, Dolby, Disney licensing.

name: White-label
blurb: let others put their brand on your product; maximize your capacity, offload their marketing. contract manufacturers, private-label.

name: Solution provider / Full coverage
blurb: cover the whole domain so you become indispensable. Salesforce, SAP.

name: Supermarket / Everything under one roof
blurb: one-stop shop; economies of scope. Amazon, Walmart.

name: Long tail
blurb: forget blockbusters; aggregate many niche items. Amazon, Spotify, Netflix catalog.

name: Vertical integration
blurb: control the whole chain; maximize efficiency, minimize dependencies. Tesla, Apple silicon, Luxottica.

name: Layer player / Specialization
blurb: do one slice of the chain better than anyone. TSMC, Stripe, Twilio.

name: Negative working capital / Cash-first
blurb: get paid before you pay suppliers; run on the float. Dell, Costco, Amazon, Berkshire (insurance float).

name: Pull-based / Demand-driven
blurb: produce reactively; stay nimble in fast markets. Toyota (JIT), Zara/Inditex.

name: Uptime / Availability SLA
blurb: sell guaranteed reliability at a premium. Salesforce, UPS, cloud infra.

name: Mass customization
blurb: personalized products at mass-production cost. Nike By You, Dell configure-to-order.

name: Recycling / Waste-to-value
blurb: turn waste into revenue. Patagonia Worn Wear, scrap/circular models.

name: Crowdsourcing
blurb: tap the crowd's collective wisdom, often via a prize. LEGO Ideas, Duolingo, Waze.

name: Open innovation / Collaboration
blurb: co-create value with partners; good ideas come from anywhere. P&G Connect+Develop.

name: Open source (give product, sell service)
blurb: free product, paid service/support; community as marketing + dev force. Red Hat, GitLab, HashiCorp.

name: User-generated content / design
blurb: let customers create what you sell; tap collective creativity, offload risk. YouTube, Roblox, Wikipedia.

name: Prosumer
blurb: turn customers into producers; the user base becomes a resource. YouTube creators, Etsy sellers.

name: Loyalty / Rewards
blurb: reward repeat behavior, build emotional lock-in, make switching hurt. Starbucks, Amex, Sephora.

name: Lock-in / Switching costs
blurb: make leaving costly; engineer durable dependencies. ERP systems, Apple ecosystem.

name: Auction
blurb: let the market set the price via bidding. eBay, Copart, CME, Google Ads.

name: Cross-sell / Bundling
blurb: reuse assets and relationships to sell across categories. Amazon, Amex, Berkshire.

name: Reverse innovation / Frugal
blurb: build for emerging markets first, then adapt up-market. GE (emerging-market medical), Jio.

name: Self-service
blurb: let customers do the work; pass on the savings. IKEA, ATMs, self-checkout.

name: Bottom of the pyramid / Volume
blurb: profit from volume at the base of the market. Unilever sachets, Jio.

name: Revenue sharing
blurb: split profits with partners or rivals; grow the pie. app stores, ad revenue share.

name: Experience-led / Experiential
blurb: sell the experience and the emotional value, not just the product. Disney, Starbucks, Airbnb.

name: Franchising
blurb: clone the model; others take the risk, you collect royalties. McDonald's, Subway, 7-Eleven.
